card.occupation: Not currently working. Formerly an administrative assistant and receptionist, most recently at a GP surgery in Walsall. She left about three years ago due to ill health and now receives disability-related benefits.
card.education_detail: Completed matric and an FA (intermediate) in Mirpur, Pakistan, before moving to the UK at 21. Took ESOL classes at Walsall College, then an NVQ Level 2 in Business Administration in her early thirties. She started an AAT bookkeeping course but never finished it.
card.household: Lives in a rented two-bed terrace with her partner Tariq, a taxi driver she had a nikah with four years ago. They never registered a civil marriage, so on paper they are cohabiting. Her younger son Zain (17, at sixth form) lives with them. Her daughter Aleena (22) lives in Birmingham. She divorced the children's father about eight years ago.
card.cultural_background: Born in Mirpur, Azad Kashmir, and came to England in 2000 after an arranged first marriage. She is a Muslim who prays when she can and fasts in Ramadan if her health allows, though she is relaxed about some things. She speaks Pahari/Mirpuri and Urdu at home and English with her son. The divorce caused some distance from her ex-husband's family, and a few aunties still gossip about her living with Tariq.
card.professional_persona: Liked front-desk work: answering phones, booking appointments, calming down irate patients. Good with people, much less good with filing and deadlines. She sometimes let paperwork pile up and smoothed it over with charm. She still knows how the NHS appointment systems work and helps relatives with forms.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty at all. She used to walk round the Arboretum but now her joints limit her. She half-watches cricket when Pakistan play because Tariq and Zain have it on.
card.arts_persona: Watches Pakistani dramas on YouTube most evenings and has opinions about the characters. She enjoys old Lata Mangeshkar and Nusrat songs. She doesn't go to galleries or theatre.
card.travel_persona: Has been back to Mirpur a handful of times, the last trip before COVID. She would love to do Umrah properly and talks about it, but money and health keep pushing it back. She has done day trips to Blackpool and Weston with family.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Mirpuri home food (saag, aloo gosht, daal) but less than she used to because standing is painful. On bad days Tariq brings takeaway or they have toast and chai. She buys mithai from Soho Road for Eid and calls a bread roll a bap.
hobbies_and_interests: online shopping for suits and abayas, often returning them
doing online surveys for a bit of extra money
looking after her balcony-less windowsill of plants, badly
skills: booking systems and basic Microsoft Word
translating Urdu and Pahari for relatives at appointments
talking her way out of late fees and parking fines
card.career_goals: Says she'd like to go back to part-time reception work 'when my health is better', maybe a few mornings a week, but has no concrete plan. Privately she is unsure it will happen.
card.voice: Soft, unhurried, slightly quiet voice with a South Asian accent layered over a light Black Country/Walsall lilt picked up over 25 years. Fluent English, with occasional Urdu words slipped in ('acha', 'theek hai') and the odd rearranged phrase. Uses 'erm' a lot and 'you know' as a tag, and says 'give it me' naturally. Agrees readily ('yeah, yeah, that's right') and seldom contradicts. In silences she waits rather than filling them, then gives a short answer, and expands only if gently prompted.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, sometimes a capital at the start because her phone does it. Few apostrophes (dont, im), commas used loosely or not at all, and the occasional autocorrect slip. Short answers like 'yes i agree with that' or 'not really sure tbh'. Sometimes types 'ok' or 'k'.
card.with_strangers: Polite, warm but reserved. She smiles a lot and lets the other person lead. She tends to say what she thinks they want to hear and may slightly polish her situation, for example describing herself as 'between jobs'. She opens up more if the person is friendly and unrushed.
small_things: Zain eating everything in the fridge
the bus being late again on the Wednesbury Road
the weather making her joints worse
a parcel she needs to send back
deeper_things: her rheumatoid arthritis and type 2 diabetes and how tiring they are
the end of her first marriage and how hard the years after were
feeling judged by some people in the community for living with Tariq
worrying about money and benefits reassessments
missing her mother, who still lives in Mirpur and is getting older
feeling a bit useless since she stopped working
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, as the laptop sits on her lap on the settee. Warm yellow light from a ceiling lamp, plus grey daylight from a window to the left that leaves one side of her face a little brighter. She is a South Asian woman in her mid-forties with a round face, tired eyes with faint dark circles, and a polite closed-mouth smile. A loose black chiffon dupatta is draped over her head, with some dark hair showing at the front. She wears a maroon cotton shalwar kameez with a grey cardigan over it, and no glasses. Behind her is a beige wall with a framed gold Ayat al-Kursi calligraphy, part of a cream net curtain, and the corner of a brown leather settee with a folded fleece blanket and a phone charger cable trailing over the arm.
